newsitem.title: USA: Ford talking with Huizenga, others on Budget.
newsitem.headline: Ford talking with Huizenga, others on Budget.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Thursday it is in talks with H. Wayne Huizenga, chief executive of Republic Industries Inc, among others about Budget Rent A Car, the sixth-largest U.S. rental car agency.
"We are looking for new owners to come in and manage Budget Rent A Car," said Ford spokesman Chris Vinyard.
Huizenga is "among a number of parties that Ford is talking with" about Budget, he said.
Hertz Corp, Ford's other rental car agency, is not involved in the discussions, Vinyard said.
Republic was not immediately available for comment.

The automaker said Wednesday it may sell its interests in Budget, which it does not own outright, but controls through a common stock purchase option. Ford declined to comment specifically on a report that it plans to sell Budget to Team Rental Group Inc, a Florida-based Budget licensee.
Wall Street analysts said they expected Ford to sell Budget, and perhaps Hertz, as well, joining other automakers in exiting the battered rental car business.
"We have been in discussions with investors, but there has been no decision reached with any parties at this point," said Budget Rent A Car spokeswoman Kimberly Mulcahy on Thursday.
Republic, based in Atlanta, on Monday agreed to acquire National Car Rental System Inc from a private investor group. The group had purchased National from General Motors Corp in 1995.
Late last year, Republic bought Alamo Rent-A-Car Inc.
Republic spokesman Ron Castel on Thursday said: "We were talking to them (Ford) earlier. But we currently have no plans to acquire another car rental company."
Chrysler Corp in 1994 sold off Snappy Car Rental, but still owns Dollar Rent-A-Car and Thrifty Rent-A-Car.
Analysts speculated this week that Chrysler may sell Dollar, the seventh-largest U.S. rental car firm, to HFS Inc, a New Jersey real estate and hotel concern.
When it bought General Motors' 29-percent interest in Avis Inc in June last year, HFS said it intended to buy another rental car agency.
